lines.explanation: Read-only profile check is active regardless of resolution status of underlying entities (both resolved here).
Read-only catch-up on #engineering is active; the channel is resolved.

Read-only search for channels discussing 'this topic' is active despite the referent set being underspecified; underspecification affects what response is appropriate, not whether the read-only action is active.

This is a conditional gate over the state-changing channel-creation step; the condition itself is evaluated as part of the workflow and is active since it depends on the read-only search outcome, which is active.

Creating a new channel is state-changing and gated on the L3/L4 condition ('if there isn't a dedicated space yet'). The linked grounding obligation (card /3, 'Resolve channels already discussing the session's topic') is underspecified: two competing readings yield different candidate sets (empty vs. {general, engineering}), and the prompt does not disambiguate which topic is meant. Per rule 4, a state-changing action whose linked grounding obligation is underspecified is marked inactive.

Posting a heads-up in #core-infra is state-changing but its grounding obligation (resolving #core-infra) is resolved to C_INFRA, and the semantic content (a debugging heads-up) is derivable from context, satisfying rule 6.

Reacting with a thumbs up is state-changing. The linked grounding obligation (card /5, resolving 'Aisha's earlier great message') is underspecified: six candidate messages exist and the prompt does not delegate the choice. Per rule 4, this makes the action inactive.

Removing a person from a project channel is state-changing. Both linked grounding obligations (card /6, resolving the departed person; card /7, resolving the project channel) are underspecified with no enumerated candidate sets and no named identity. Per rule 4, this makes the action inactive.
